Remark
[Einstein metrics in harmonic coordinates are smooth]

Source: petersen:page-0425, petersen:page-0426 ↗ lem:pet-ch11-laplacian-ricci-harmonic-coords ↗ cor:pet-ch11-higher-schauder-estimates For an Einstein metric $\Ric _{ij}=(n-1)kg_{ij}$, subsection 2.3 reads $\tfrac 12\Delta g_{ij}=-(n-1)kg_{ij}-Q(g,\partial g)$, which makes sense once $g_{ij}\in C^1$ and, after multiplying by a test function and integrating by parts, can be interpreted weakly. If $g_{ij}\in C^{1,\alpha }$ the right side lies in some $C^\beta $, so subsection 2.2 gives $g_{ij}\in C^{2,\beta }$; bootstrapping shows $g_{ij}\in C^\infty $ (in fact real-analytic). Hence any metric that is, in harmonic coordinates, a weak solution of the Einstein equation is automatically smooth.
